stem: Which combination lists the main body parts of a Lumen Moth?

options.text: Head, compound eyes, respiratory spiracles, and feathery sensory filaments.
Specialized thorax, internal glands, and translucent chitinous shell.
Head, specialized thorax, abdomen, sensory antennae, and delicate wings.
Abdomen, muscular tissues, lumium glands, and a liquid-siphoning proboscis.

stem: What role does the Lumen Moth's thorax play in producing luminescence?

options.text: It acts as a biological engine where oxygen and lumium mix under muscular control to emit rhythmic illumination.
It siphons synthetic nectar which then travels to the lower segments to produce cold energy.
It contains sensory filaments that track chemical trails to ignite the internal combustion chamber.
It converts absorbed solar radiation from the prismatic panels into visible enzymatic reactions.

stem: How can a Keeper tell the sex of a Lumen Moth by looking at its antennae?

options.text: Females feature feathery appendages for finding ideal egg-laying spots, while males have needle-like points for detecting food.
Males have swollen, pulsing appendages, while females have completely translucent sensory shells.
Females grow broad filaments to track airborne moon-root spores, while males have slender stalks to locate dispensers.
Males possess wide, comb-like filaments for finding mates, while females have thin, smooth points for assessing climate.

stem: In what order does a Lumen Moth progress through its developmental phases?

options.text: Feeding drift, mating chase, resting cluster.
Dormant Egg, Crawling Nymph, Glowing Imago.
Inactive sphere, segmented caterpillar, feathery adult.
Suspension, metamorphosis, continuous photogenesis.

stem: What biological changes occur inside the chrysalis as a Nymph becomes an Imago?

options.text: The segmented body rapidly consumes caloric reserves to expand its mass and shed its restrictive outer layer.
The creature halts all metabolic activity for a month to survive extreme external temperature drops.
The organism dissolves into fundamental cells and rebuilds into a winged adult equipped with lumium glands.
The internal chemistry shifts to break down iron-rich additives, causing the newly formed wings to dry and expand.

stem: A Keeper places a fresh batch of Dormant Eggs on an Iron-Oak branch and holds the glass house steady at 40 Vels. After how many days should the Nymphs emerge?

options.text: Fourteen days.
Eighteen days.
Ten days.
Twenty-eight days.

stem: A heater malfunction keeps a nursery of newly laid Dormant Eggs at a steady 38 Vels instead of the standard 40 Vels. How long will incubation take under these conditions?

options.text: Fourteen days.
Twelve days.
Twenty-eight days.
Eighteen days.

stem: What does the term photogenesis mean when applied to Lepidoptera luminis?

options.text: The momentary flashes of intensity used to ward off natural predators in darkened mountain valleys.
The uninterrupted biological generation of visible light fueled by internal enzymatic processes.
The daily absorption of external radiation to produce a cold glow throughout the evening.
The rapid mass exhaustion resulting from extreme heat exposure inside the enclosed architectural space.

stem: How do lumium and air interact inside the moth to produce its glow?

options.text: A specialized moon-root additive ferments inside the gut, creating a glowing gas that escapes through abdominal spiracles.
Metallic catalysts break down sugar-sap, generating a thermal reaction that ignites the central biological chamber.
Breathable oxygen contacts diet-derived lumium in the glands, causing rapid oxidation that releases cold light.
Involuntary muscular spasms compress the insect's inner fluids, converting kinetic energy into rhythmic visible flashes.

stem: Why is it vital that the oxidation of lumium releases energy without generating heat?

options.text: Producing warmth would fatally cook the insect's internal tissues from within.
Elevated body heat would trigger a premature Frost Moon hibernation in the middle of a breeding cycle.
Warmth would evaporate the circulatory fluids required to expand the Glowing Imago's delicate wings.
Heat generation attracts Glass-Borer Beetles that destroy the structural integrity of the Iron-Oak frame.

stem: During a nocturnal observation, a Keeper sees the swarm's glow stuttering and flashing chaotically rather than pulsing smoothly. What dietary issue should the Keeper diagnose?

options.text: The environmental pressure has dropped by more than five Torr-Pascs, causing respiratory distress.
The glass house temperature has reached 55 Vels, inducing a frenzied state of swarm panic.
The synthetic nectar has spoiled and smells of burnt almonds, poisoning the Glowing Imagoes.
The moths lack sufficient iron in their nectar to stabilize the lumium oxidation reaction.

stem: How many days does one complete Lumen Moth breeding cycle take under standard conditions?

options.text: Fourteen days.
Twenty-eight days.
Twenty-one days.
Thirty days.

stem: What happens to the swarm's reproductive activity when the Frost Moon arrives in the tenth month?

options.text: Shifting atmospheric pressure induces a rapid mating chase that dramatically increases population numbers.
Altered celestial light spectra cause females to lay sterile eggs and suffer premature wing deterioration.
The moths enter metabolic dormancy and stop laying eggs completely for thirty days.
Crawling Nymphs begin cannibalizing unhatched eggs due to heavily depleted biological energy reserves.

stem: The tenth month arrives, but abnormal weather prevents the swarm from entering its natural Frost Moon dormancy. How should the Keeper intervene?

options.text: Gradually cool the glass house from 42 Vels to 35 Vels over a week while diluting the nectar supply.
Immediately drop the internal climate to 12 Vels to freeze the remaining Dormant Eggs.
Increase the heat to 55 Vels and restrict all moon-root access until the adults enter dormancy.
Quarantine the swarm for 21 days and wash the gravity drip dispensers with V-Scrub solution.

stem: Which set names the four routine flight behaviors observed in a healthy Lumen Moth swarm?

options.text: Spiral descent, swarm aggregation, rapid ricocheting, and erratic darting.
Undulating movement, upper corner packing, downward corkscrews, and blind flying.
Mating chase, canopy patrol, sudden panic, and metabolic suspension.
Feeding drift, mating chase, resting cluster, and canopy patrol.

stem: Why would a swarm of Glowing Imagoes begin flying in tight downward corkscrews toward the floor?

options.text: A rapid drop in internal pressure is forcing the insects away from the upper prismatic panels.
Starvation of moon-root in their diet is disrupting their buoyancy and causing wing muscle spasms.
Toxic gas buildup from over-fermented nectar is paralyzing their primary respiratory spiracles.
An incursion of Glass-Borer Beetles is driving them to seek cover among the lower branches.

stem: During a mountain storm, internal pressure falls by 7 Torr-Pascs in an hour, and the moths pack tightly into the highest glass angles. What should the Keeper do?

options.text: Open the floor vents to allow trapped daytime heat to escape before the swarm panics.
Immediately restock all gravity drip dispensers with freshly crushed moon-root.
Pump air into the chamber with the manual Draft-Bellows until internal pressure equalizes.
Dim the ambient illumination to calm the frenzied insects and stop them from hitting the glass.

stem: Which trio of materials is permitted by the Keepers' Guild for building the frame and foundation of a Glass House?

options.text: Refined steel, soda-lime glass, and treated pine timber.
Cured Iron-Oak, quarried Alabaster-Stone, and spun Copper-Resin.
Spun Copper-Resin, galvanized iron, and silver-infused quartz.
Quarried Alabaster-Stone, tempered brass, and cured Iron-Oak.

stem: Why do Guild architectural rules mandate cured Iron-Oak rather than refined steel for primary load-bearing pillars?

options.text: Iron-Oak insulates against thermal shocks, avoids magnetic disorientation of male antennae, and naturally repels Glass-Borer Beetles.
Refined steel reacts chemically with V-Scrub vapors to release a gas that turns moth light a sickly green.
Iron-Oak reflects thirty percent more bioluminescence downward than steel while filtering out solar ultraviolet radiation.
Refined steel cannot support the weight of wedge-cut prismatic panels when the roof angle exceeds thirty-five degrees.

stem: A Master Luminary reviews a blueprint for a new Glass House and notes north-wall Iron-Oak pillars spaced 16 feet apart, a 40-degree roof pitch, and a supported central ridge post. What flaw must be corrected?

options.text: The roof pitch must be lowered below 25 degrees so snow adds stabilizing weight to the canopy.
The central ridge post must be removed so the Copper-Resin ribs can flex freely in mountain winds.
The north-wall pillars must be moved to sit no more than 12 feet apart to prevent the overhead ribs from sagging.
The Alabaster-Stone foundation must be replaced with spun Copper-Resin piers along the south wall.

stem: Where are the three sets of ventilation openings positioned in a standard Glass House?

options.text: Subterranean floor ducts, south-wall prismatic louvers, and corner chimney flues.
North-wall roof eaves, central pillar check-valves, and west-wall doorway transoms.
Perimeter foundation grates, twelve-foot collar beams, and south-facing silvered hatches.
Low north-wall louvers near the floor, mid-level east-west wall slots, and the high apex ridge beneath the canopy.

stem: How does excessive internal wind speed affect a swarm of Glowing Imagoes?

options.text: Currents above three miles per hour overpower their wings, scatter routine flight patterns, and strip heat from their thoraxes.
Strong drafts force excess oxygen into their abdominal spiracles, causing their light output to spike past thirty Candons.
Rapid airflow dries out the Sponge Troughs on the lower branches and triggers an immediate spiral descent toward the floor.
Cross-breezes cause the feathery antennae of females to tangle together during the nocturnal mating chase.

stem: An alpine squall causes the Glass House pressure gauge to drop rapidly from 140 Torr-Pascs toward 132 Torr-Pascs. In what order should the Keeper use the ventilation controls and Draft-Bellows?

options.text: Open the apex ridge fully, attach the Draft-Bellows to the south louvers, and pump at sixty strokes per minute.
Shut all north intake louvers, unlatch the mid-level slots, and pump the Draft-Bellows until pressure reaches 180 Torr-Pascs.
Latch the mid-level slots and apex ridge while leaving north louvers cracked one inch, then pump the Draft-Bellows at the north pillar valve at twenty strokes per minute back to 140 Torr-Pascs.
Disconnect the misting pump, open the floor drains, and operate the Draft-Bellows in figure-eight sweeps three feet below the canopy.

stem: What dual optical roles do the wedge-cut prismatic panels in the upper vault perform?

options.text: They block ninety-five percent of ultraviolet rays by day and vent excess biological heat into the night sky.
They diffuse harsh daylight into soft violet-indigo bands and reflect upward moth luminescence back down at night.
They focus midday sunlight onto the brewing vats and polarize moonlight during the tenth-month Frost Moon.
They magnify the image of approaching Glass-Borer Beetles and absorb excess moisture from the misting nozzles.

stem: How does Lunar-Tinted Glass protect the swarm from intense afternoon sunshine?

options.text: Its wedge-shaped quartz ridges bend incoming light around the central Iron-Oak pillars toward the floor.
A layer of spun Copper-Resin on the inner face absorbs heat and transfers it into the Alabaster-Stone footing.
Its thick soda-lime core freezes at twelve Vels, creating a frost barrier that blocks all visible light.
Suspended trace silver particles form an internal lattice that scatters ultraviolet and infrared rays while passing cool silver-blue light.

stem: A hailstorm shatters a lower wall pane on the south side of a Glass House. Which pane and orientation must the Keeper install into the Copper-Resin muntins?

options.text: A certified sheet of silver-infused Lunar-Tinted Glass with its slightly concave silvered face oriented toward the outside.
A wedge-cut quartz prismatic panel with its faceted ridges facing inward toward the feeding dispensers.
A double-thick clear soda-lime pane bedded in Iron-Oak sap with its smooth face toward the interior.
A sheet of Lunar-Tinted Glass coated in V-Scrub solution with its concave face oriented toward the north wall.

stem: Why must Keepers wash the interior facets of the overhead prismatic panels with diluted V-Scrub every month?

options.text: To dissolve the silver lattice buildup that otherwise turns the panels opaque over time.
To keep the quartz facets clean so they continue reflecting nearly thirty percent more bioluminescence back down to the lower branches.
To neutralize the burnt-almond odor that accumulates near the apex exhaust ridge during fermentation.
To cool the canopy glass from fifty-five Vels down to forty-two Vels before the dusk transition begins.

stem: What temperature range must a Keeper maintain inside the Glass House during the one-hour transition at sunset?

options.text: Between 35 Vels and 40 Vels.
Between 12 Vels and 35 Vels.
Between 41 Vels and 44 Vels.
Between 45 Vels and 55 Vels.

stem: Why is active cooling performed at nightfall rather than daybreak in a Glass House?

options.text: At nightfall, stored solar warmth radiating from the stone foundation combines with heat from thousands of waking, flapping moths.
The chemical oxidation of lumium inside the thorax releases intense thermal energy only during the first hour after sunset.
At daybreak, the Lunar-Tinted Glass automatically super-cools the enclosure by reflecting early morning frost.
Nightfall cooling is required to freeze the synthetic nectar in the gravity drip dispensers before the moths feed.

stem: During a weekly instrument check, a Keeper places a Vels-Thermometer into a chilled copper beaker of unfermented synthetic nectar. Just as slush crystals form across the surface, the thermometer reads 15 Vels. How should the Keeper adjust the instrument?

options.text: Add crushed moon-root to the beaker until the mercury rises to 40 Vels.
Warm the beaker to 42 Vels and set the pointer to match the wall hygrometer.
Submerge the thermometer in V-Scrub solution and lock the screw at 14 Candons.
Turn the brass screw at the tube's base until the pointer drops to the 12-Vel mark, then lock the nut.

stem: What relative atmospheric moisture range is required to maximize the lifespan and wing health of adult Lumen Moths?

options.text: Between 40 percent and 45 percent.
Between 65 percent and 70 percent.
Between 80 percent and 95 percent.
Between 50 percent and 55 percent.

stem: How does atmospheric moisture inside the Glass House influence the brightness of the swarm's glow?

options.text: Water vapor reacts directly with airborne moon-root spores to create a glowing mist around the canopy.
High moisture cools the translucent chitin shell, allowing blue light waves to pass through without refraction.
Proper moisture keeps internal tracheal linings filmed with water for oxygen diffusion, whereas overly dry or wet air blocks oxygen from reaching the lumium glands.
Dry airbelow fifty percent accelerates oxygen uptake through the spiracles, doubling an adult's output to twenty-eight Candons.

stem: What physical damage occurs to the swarm if relative humidity remains above 70 percent for more than six hours?

options.text: Chitin scales flake off the wings and shorten the adult lifespan to less than ten days.
Water droplets bead on the feathery antennae of males and weigh them down, blinding their pheromone receptors.
The moths pack tightly into the upper glass corners as if experiencing a sudden pressure drop.
The tracheal tubes inside the thorax rupture from excessive osmotic pressure during the mating chase.

stem: A Keeper notices the Glass House hygrometer has dropped to 48 percent humidity, while the hydraulic log for the misting pump shows line pressure spiking to 125 Torr-Pascs. What action should the Keeper take?

options.text: Replace the torn leather gasket inside the main water pump and patch the split copper supply pipe.
Use the Draft-Bellows to force extra air into the water reservoir until line pressure returns to 90 Torr-Pascs.
Open the low north louvers and high apex ridge to draw damp mountain fog into the chamber.
Shut the main water valve, unscrew the clogged overhead brass nozzle tips, and soak them in V-Scrub solution for ten minutes.

stem: Which collection of substances constitutes the five mandatory ingredients for synthetic nectar?

options.text: Crushed moon-root, spring water, raw sugar-sap, copper-flower petals, and mineral sea-ash.
Powdered silver, fermented Iron-Oak sap, purified water, sea salt, and moon-root pulp.
Crushed moon-root, distilled alcohol, copper shavings, sugar crystals, and river water.
Iron-Oak resin, mineral sea-ash, boiled nectar, honey-water, and cobalt powder.

stem: How does the ingestion of prepared moon-root enable the insect to glow?

options.text: Its starchy sugars ferment in the abdomen to generate high pneumatic pressure behind the wings.
Alkaloid proteins within the tuber travel to the thorax to be converted into lumium for oxidation.
Its metallic trace minerals react directly with digestive enzymes to emit ultraviolet radiation.
The tuber coats the insect's antennae with reflective crystals that scatter ambient glasshouse light.

stem: A glass house holds exactly 500 adult Glowing Imagoes. What volumes of sugar-sap and mountain spring water must a Keeper blend for their daily nourishment?

options.text: 100 Drams of sugar-sap and 500 Drams of spring water.
300 Drams of sugar-sap and 900 Drams of spring water.
200 Drams of sugar-sap and 600 Drams of spring water.
400 Drams of sugar-sap and 400 Drams of spring water.

stem: What is the proper procedural sequence when preparing a fresh batch of synthetic nectar?

options.text: Boil the spring water, add crushed moon-root, ferment for twelve hours, and strain into dispensers.
Dissolve minerals in cold water, heat the kettle to fifty Vels, and stir in raw moon-root paste.
Soak moon-root for 12 hours, heat water, dissolve sap and minerals, infuse strained liquid, and cool.
Ferment raw sap for two days, bring to a rolling boil, add moon-root liquid, and filter through silk.

stem: Why must the brewing kettle be kept strictly below 40 Vels while simmering synthetic nectar?

options.text: Excessive heat boils off the volatile alcohol before fermentation can even begin in the casks.
Temperatures above this threshold denature the sensitive moon-root alkaloids and ruin photogenesis.
Heating beyond this level causes copper minerals to precipitate into an insoluble black sludge.
Elevated temperatures trigger rapid oxidation that ignites the sugary fluid inside the copper vat.

stem: A Keeper observes persistent relative humidity of 76 percent inside the enclosure. How should the standard nectar recipe be altered?

options.text: Double the soaking duration of the moon-root and reduce the boiling temperature to 25 Vels.
Dilute the mixture with an additional 100 Drams of spring water to prevent nozzle blockages.
Replace the liquid water entirely with mineral sea-ash powder to absorb airborne condensation.
Increase sugar-sap by ten percent to 220 Drams and decrease starting water by 50 Drams.

stem: What is the minimum resting duration required for a cask of standard nectar to ferment before use?

options.text: Forty-eight hours.
Twenty-four hours.
Seventy-two hours.
Twelve hours.

stem: What vital biochemical transformation occurs during the 48-hour resting period of synthetic nectar?

options.text: Complex sap sugars convert into simple monosaccharides and bind with alkaloids into an organo-luminescent fluid.
Atmospheric oxygen saturates the mixture to produce a steady baseline glow of fourteen Candons.
Dissolved copper particles form microscopic crystalline lattices that neutralize harmful bacteria.
The liquid ferments into a heavy, viscous resin suitable for resealing glasshouse window seams.

stem: Which sensory warning signals that a resting nectar vat has undergone catastrophic over-fermentation?

options.text: A sweet fragrance of flowering clover paired with bright blue sediment.
A clear, thin consistency that fails to coat a wooden stirring paddle.
A sharp scent resembling burnt almonds accompanied by frothy gray surface scum.
A heavy sulfurous stench accompanied by dark amber discoloration.

stem: Which pair represents the two primary apparatuses utilized to deliver liquid feed to a captive colony?

options.text: Pneumatic spray nozzles and ceramic feeding cups.
Gravity Drip Dispensers and Sponge Troughs.
Capillary wicks and pressurized misting tubes.
Unglazed earthenware pots and hanging copper basins.

stem: Why are Sponge Troughs preferred over Gravity Drip Dispensers when rearing immature Crawling Nymphs?

options.text: They allow continuous twenty-four-hour feeding without requiring manual refilling by Keepers.
They eliminate open droplets and standing liquid, preventing wingless young from drowning.
They maintain a higher temperature of forty Vels through natural biological fermentation.
They release airborne vapor that accelerates the metamorphosis into the chrysalis phase.

stem: A Keeper needs to install a new feeding station for emerging Crawling Nymphs along a busy nursery pathway. Where and how should it be placed?

options.text: Suspended from the roof trusses fifteen feet up, using copper wires and an automatic drip valve.
Buried in the foundation floor gravel directly beneath the central ventilation chimney.
Fastened to a lower branch within 3 feet of the floor with copper brackets, holding a soaked sponge flush with the rim.
Hooked onto the south-facing glass frames where direct afternoon sunlight keeps the tray warm.

stem: What physical signs indicate that an adult swarm is suffering from severe moon-root deficiency?

options.text: Frenzied flight at fifty-five Vels accompanied by rapid ricocheting off canopy glass.
Swarm packing in upper building corners and refusal to feed from gravity drippers.
Helpless spiral descent flights toward the ground, shriveled bodies, and light fading below 3 Candons.
Erratic flashing of emerald-green luminescence and premature shedding of wing scales.

stem: What chromatic effect does an insufficient supply of dietary iron produce in the bioluminescence of the moth?

options.text: The normal silver-blue radiance shifts into an erratic, greenish light due to misfiring oxidation.
The light turns a deep, saturated violet as the insect's core body temperature spikes.
The glow shifts to a bright amber color that burns through the glass of the storage flasks.
The output becomes completely clear and invisible, perceptible only to calibrated Candon-meters.

stem: A colony displays erratic greenish flashing and dim output. How should the Keeper structure their seven-day recovery plan?

options.text: Withhold all nectar for 48 hours, then reintroduce standard feed diluted with fifty percent water.
Cool the glass house to thirty-five Vels to force an early 30-day Frost Moon dormancy.
Purge and clean drippers, supply doubled moon-root with extra iron-rich sap, and monitor until output hits 14 Candons.
Mist the canopy with diluted V-Scrub solution while feeding unfermented sap from high-capacity drippers.

stem: What harmful substance is released when resting nectar is allowed to ferment beyond its safe limits in warm conditions?

options.text: A caustic liquid that dissolves the silver lattice embedded within south-facing glass panes.
A toxic gas that corrodes the iron bands securing elevated gravity drip dispensers.
A dense acidic vapor that causes unhatched eggs to hatch two weeks ahead of schedule.
An oily residue that clogs the porous cells of terrestrial sponge troughs within hours.

stem: Why must crushed moon-root soak for twelve hours in cold spring water prior to the boiling process?

options.text: To soften tough exterior fibers so the mixture can pass through fine sponge dispensers.
To extract vital alkaloid proteins safely without breaking down their sensitive heat rings.
To activate the dormant yeast spores naturally adhering to the skin of the raw tuber.
To neutralize natural acidic poisons that would otherwise corrode the copper brewing kettle.

stem: Which set of equipment must a harvest team bring to the upper walkways before collecting luminescence?

options.text: Draft-Bellows, Vels-Thermometer, and unglazed earthenware jars.
Lunar-Net, evacuated copper collector manifold, and portable pneumatic transfer siphon.
Sponge Troughs, brass balance scales, and Gravity Drip Dispensers.
Torr-Pasc pressure gauge, copper kettle, and wooden stirring paddle.

stem: How should a harvester execute the Sweep Method to collect ambient light under the roof?

options.text: Execute wide, continuous figure-eight patterns precisely three feet below the canopy vents.
Thrust the net rapidly upward into resting clusters clinging along the central Iron-Oak beam.
Drag the net along the Alabaster-Stone floor beneath the lowest intake louvers.
Hold the net stationary against the south-facing Lunar-Tinted Glass panels for sixty minutes.

stem: Why must harvesters maintain an exact three-foot clearance below the ceiling panels while sweeping?

options.text: Moving too close disrupts the low north-wall draft and lowers pressure below 140 Torr-Pascs.
Direct contact with the roof vents allows toxic over-fermented gas to enter the intake collar.
Approaching too close to the prismatic panels risks cracking the glass from net static buildup.
Sweeping near the top forces the swarm into sudden fifty-five Vel thermal panic.

stem: While conducting a practice sweep, an Apprentice sees several Glowing Imagoes veer toward the oncoming Lunar-Net hoop. How should the Apprentice react?

options.text: Jerk the net backward sharply and drop the Iron-Oak handle to the walkway floor.
Wave the net in rapid circular motions to generate high wind and scatter the insects.
Pump the Draft-Bellows toward the insects to blow them into the lower feeding troughs.
Slowly angle the net rim parallel to the airflow so the insects' own wake carries them past safely.

stem: What is the maximum liquid capacity of a standard Lumium Flask when filled to the boundary mark?

options.text: Exactly 50 Drams.
Exactly 200 Drams.
Exactly 14 Drams.
Exactly 100 Drams.

stem: Why must harvested luminescence be stored inside vacuum-sealed containers?

options.text: Contact with atmospheric oxygen causes rapid runaway oxidation that destroys the compound in hours.
Exposure to ambient humidity causes the liquid to thicken and crystallize into unusable stone.
The fluid reacts with airborne nitrogen to generate toxic fumes that corrode glass walls.
Vacuum pressure is necessary to keep the internal liquid temperature frozen at twelve Vels.

stem: A warehouse inspector finds a Lumium Flask weeping fluid around its collar threads. What materials and steps resolve the leak?

options.text: Submerge the flask in pure V-Scrub solution and solder the neck shut with copper wire.
Cool to 35 Vels, clean threads with damp linen, apply sugar-sap tree resin, and torque clamp to 15 inch-pounds.
Warm the flask to 55 Vels, wipe the collar with raw nectar, and tighten the valve by hand.
Pour the contents into an unglazed earthenware jar and seal the top with Alabaster-Stone dust.

stem: What is a Candon according to the official definitions of the Keepers Guild?

options.text: The amount of pressure exerted by one hundred strokes of the manual Draft-Bellows.
The volume of synthetic nectar consumed by fifty adult moths during a twenty-four-hour period.
The fundamental unit of light measurement, equal to the luminous flux of a standard tallow candle.
The thermal unit required to raise one Dram of mountain water by one Vel on the thermometer.

stem: How does a Candon-meter convert ambient luminescence into a numerical reading on its dial?

options.text: A selenium plate converts diffused light into an electric current that deflects an analog pointer.
A miniature mercury column expands when exposed to the thermal radiation of bioluminescent photons.
A rotating optical prism splits incoming beams into colors counted by a mechanical clockwork gear.
A small chamber of dormant lumium reacts with ambient light and changes internal pressure.

stem: A harvest crew fills 60 standard Lumium Flasks to capacity. A calibrated meter records an average saturation of 12 Candons per Dram. What is the total yield?

options.text: 720 Candons.
12,000 Candons.
18,000 Candons.
36,000 Candons.

stem: What protective eye gear is legally mandated for all personnel participating in the Luminous Harvest?

options.text: Tinted goggles with a Candon-rating of at least 200 Cd.
Clear quartz lenses treated with an anti-static silver coating.
Darkened leather masks featuring narrow pinhole slits.
Amber-tinted spectacles rated for fifty Torr-Pascs of impact resistance.

stem: What physiological effect occurs when human eyes are exposed to raw, un-flasked luminescence at close range?

options.text: Short-wavelength cold photons cause light-burn by bleaching retinal rhodopsin pigments, causing temporary blindness.
Infrared heat waves burn the corneal surface, causing immediate scarring and permanent vision loss.
Fine airborne silver scales settle on the lens, triggering an incurable bacterial eye infection.
Magnetic fields emitted by the lumium fluid invert the optic nerve signals for several weeks.

stem: An Apprentice accidentally views an unsealed manifold and suffers acute light-burn. What immediate first aid must be administered?

options.text: Flush eyes with diluted V-Scrub solution and seat the patient under direct noon sunlight.
Move to a blackout room, flush with chilled saline for five minutes, and apply cold moon-root compresses for 12 hours.
Drip fermented sugar-sap into the eyes and hold the patient in a room heated to 42 Vels.
Bandage the eyes with warm wool soaked in iron-rich sap and place the victim near the draft vents.

stem: Which sequence correctly names the three processing phases harvested light must complete prior to carriage?

options.text: Distillation, chemical filtration, and vacuum bottling.
Settling, acoustic stabilization, and thermal grading.
Evacuation, ultrasonic heating, and optical refraction.
Fermentation, resting, and Candon certification.

stem: How does excessive physical vibration during carriage affect stored luminescence?

options.text: It degrades stored luminescence by two percent per hour by breaking down bound molecular rings.
It raises the internal fluid temperature above 55 Vels, causing the glassware to shatter.
It causes the fluid to separate into raw iron sap and dense mineral sea-ash sediment.
It turns the glowing liquid into an acidic vapor that corrodes the brass valve threads.

stem: A Luminary prepares an official transport manifest for 40 Grade A Lumium Flasks holding 10 Candons per Dram. What details must the document contain?

options.text: The driver's name, the weight of the carriage, the number of draft horses, and the weather forecast.
The volume of spring water used in brewing, the current Torr-Pasc reading, and the harvest team roster.
The batch number, 40 flasks totaling 2,000 Drams, 20,000 Candons yield, departure timestamp, and registered seal imprint.
The age of the Iron-Oak crates, the road toll receipt, the total weight in pounds, and the guild tax exemption code.

stem: Why does a Lumium Flask risk failure if filled beyond its 50-Dram capacity?

options.text: Overfilling causes the glass walls to dissolve under extreme chemical acidity.
The fluid freezes into crystals that expand and split the outer brass cage.
Excess volume blocks the neck valve from seating flush, creating micro-fissures that allow vacuum leakage.
The additional weight unbalances the carriage cradles and increases road vibration.

stem: Which combination of visual traits identifies an adult Glass-Borer Beetle?

options.text: Two-inch length, charcoal and ochre chevrons, serrated silicate mandibles, and six golden wing tubercles.
Pale green translucent shell, feathery comb-like antennae, and a segmented abdomen without wings.
Four-inch blue body, smooth silver mouthparts, and iridescent white spots across its thorax.
One-inch black carapace, broad comb-like antennae, and a hollow proboscis for siphoning wood sap.

stem: How do Glass-Borer Beetles penetrate the structural envelope of an enclosure?

options.text: Adults bore through Alabaster-Stone foundation walls by secreting high-pressure alkaline gas.
Grubs hatch in muntin joints and dissolve window putties with acid to chew through pane seams.
Larvae hide inside hollow Iron-Oak logs during initial construction and emerge after two years.
Swarming adults fly against south-facing Lunar-Tinted Glass until the brittle panes crack.

stem: A Keeper discovers an adult Glass-Borer Beetle inside the main enclosure. What dietary mandate must be enforced immediately?

options.text: Feed the colony an exclusive diet of crushed moon-root soaked in pure mountain spring water for 48 hours.
Withhold all liquid feed for three days to starve the beetle of suitable prey.
Feed the entire moth colony an iron-heavy diet for seven continuous days to deter the predator.
Infuse synthetic nectar with diluted V-Scrub solution to poison the invading insect.

stem: How should a Keeper construct an exterior monitoring network to intercept Glass-Borer Beetles before they reach the building?

options.text: Hang vacuum-sealed Lumium Flasks every five feet along the upper roof eaves to attract beetles with light.
Sink copper pitfall traps filled with scented sap every 10 feet along the foundation beneath pitch-coated glass.
Lay sponge troughs saturated with boiling spring water around the base of all north-facing doors.
Erect a perimeter fence made of untreated steel poles spaced twelve feet apart to disrupt beetle navigation.

stem: What are the first three physical manifestations of Wing-Fade Disease in the order they develop?

options.text: Erratic flight in spiral descents, abdomen swelling, and total loss of antennal filaments.
Light turning emerald, wing margins curling upward, and chalky white spots on the thorax.
Thoracic chitin softening, light output dropping below 3 Candons, and unhatched eggs rotting.
Frenzied ricocheting off glass, antenna curling, and wings dropping off the body entirely.

stem: In what manner does tainted liquid nourishment lead to the spread of Wing-Fade Disease through a colony?

options.text: Mold toxins erode insect gut barriers so pathogens reach wing veins and transfer via communal drippers.
Excess alcohol in spoiled nectar lowers the moth's body temperature to twelve Vels, freezing the wing joints.
Bacterial spores coat the proboscis and turn airborne when the moth performs its canopy patrol flight.
Over-fermented sap produces toxic vapors that melt the delicate silver filaments on male antennae.

stem: A Journeyman detects Stage Two Wing-Fade across thirty insects. What procedural chain of action must be followed?

options.text: Obtain an isolation order from a Master Luminary, catch moths with a Lunar-Net, and isolate for 21 days.
Immediately destroy the affected insects with copper mallet strikes and ventilate the roof.
Declare an immediate quarantine, wash all moths in warm V-Scrub, and hold them in darkness for 12 hours.
Transfer the entire swarm to an unheated glass house and restrict feeding to dry sponge troughs for 14 days.

stem: What is meant by the term swarm panic when describing Lumen Moth colony behavior?

options.text: A coordinated defensive flight formation where adults pack into upper corners to avoid cold drafts.
A collective hysteria marked by chaotic, high-speed flight and collisions that cause rapid exhaustion.
A temporary cessation of movement and feeding brought on by the arrival of the Frost Moon.
A continuous downward spiral descent toward the floor caused by acute moon-root starvation.

stem: Why does an environmental temperature surge to 55 Vels trigger sudden swarm panic?

options.text: The heat evaporates all moisture from the Sponge Troughs, creating panic over the water supply.
High heat causes the Iron-Oak frame to emit acoustic vibrations that disorient female antennae.
Overheating drives erratic synaptic firing and runaway lumium oxidation, causing a frantic escape response.
Thermal expansion shatters the south-facing glass panes, allowing cold mountain winds to rush inside.

stem: A sudden heating system failure causes a colony to ricochet wildly off the canopy glass. What sequence should the Keeper execute?

options.text: Draw roof blackout shades, pull floor dampers for cool air below 40 Vels, and mist with lavender water.
Open the apex vents, ignite sulfur candles on the floor, and sweep the canopy with the Lunar-Net.
Raise internal humidity to ninety percent and pump the Draft-Bellows at sixty strokes per minute.
Direct intense light beams through prismatic panels to blind the moths into landing on the floor.

stem: What distinct scent indicates that resting nectar has degraded into a dangerous, spoiled state?

options.text: A sweet, floral fragrance of wild mountain clover.
A pungent, sharp odor resembling burnt almonds.
A damp, earthy smell similar to decaying Iron-Oak leaves.
A heavy metallic stench like molten copper and zinc.

stem: What chemical fate befalls moon-root alkaloids when synthetic nectar undergoes bacterial spoilage?

options.text: Alkaloid rings are cleaved into acidic crystals and corrosive gas that damage insect intestines.
Alkaloids bind with trace silver particles to form an insoluble metallic crust on feeding sponges.
The molecules convert into heavy sugar-sap polymers that permanently seal proboscis openings.
The active compounds oxidize spontaneously, generating intense heat that boils the liquid in the vat.

stem: A feeding trough has developed a burnt-almond smell and gray scum. How must a Keeper clean and restore the station?

options.text: Scrub the trough with pure V-Scrub solution without raw lumium, rinse with 50 Drams boiling water, and dry.
Mix V-Scrub solution directly with condensed lumium to create an effervescent disinfectant foam.
Wipe the wooden surfaces with raw sugar-sap and heat the trough to fifty-five Vels for ten minutes.
Rinse the apparatus with cold mountain water and soak the sea sponge in diluted sea-ash brine.

stem: Why is it strictly forbidden to bring V-Scrub solution into contact with uncontained lumium?

options.text: The mixture turns into an inert gray sludge that permanently fouls the Candon-meter sensors.
The chemical combination produces an intensely exothermic reaction that can shatter glass and emit fumes.
It neutralizes the cleaning power of the acid, allowing mold spores to survive inside the trough.
The interaction strips the silver lattice out of adjacent south-facing Lunar-Tinted Glass panels.

stem: At what internal pressure threshold must a Keeper initiate emergency venting procedures to save the structure?

options.text: When internal pressure exceeds 180 Torr-Pascs of atmospheric resistance.
When the barometer drops by 5 Torr-Pascs per hour during an alpine gale.
When hydraulic misting line pressure falls below 60 Torr-Pascs.
When canopy pressure reaches 140 Torr-Pascs under normal flight operations.

stem: Why must ground-level and mid-tier louvers be opened before releasing the high roof vents during an emergency surge?

options.text: Releasing the apex first causes an implosive vacuum collapse that shatters the Prismatic Panels.
Opening the lower vents first prevents Glass-Borer Beetles from being sucked inside the building.
The sudden updraft of opening roof vents first pulls all synthetic nectar out of the gravity dispensers.
Releasing the top first forces the internal temperature to spike instantly past fifty-five Vels.

stem: During a severe barometric surge, the pull-rod for the apex exhaust ridge jams shut with ice. How should the Keeper perform the manual override?

options.text: Fire the pneumatic Draft-Bellows directly at the hinge until the ice cracks under compressed air.
Heat the louver mechanism using an open torch fueled by fermented Iron-Oak sugar-sap.
Disengage the linkage pin, wedge an Iron-Oak block into the seam, strike with a mallet, and chain open.
Smash the nearest prismatic pane with a brass spanner to relieve pressure on the jammed louver leaf.

stem: Which sequence lists the four official ranks of the Keepers' Guild in proper ascending order?

options.text: Apprentice, Journeyman, Luminary, and Master Luminary.
Initiate, Harvester, Glazier, and High Luminary.
Apprentice, Keeper, Craftsman, and Grand Luminary.
Journeyman, Apprentice, Master Luminary, and Council Luminary.

stem: Which high-level regulatory action can be legally authorized only by a Master Luminary?

options.text: Signing a daily transport manifest for twenty Grade A Lumium Flasks.
Issuing an official quarantine order for an outbreak of Wing-Fade Disease.
Operating the manual Draft-Bellows during a five Torr-Pasc pressure drop.
Adjusting the baseline calibration screw on a brass Vels-Thermometer.

stem: An Apprentice discovers that a primary Iron-Oak load pillar has cracked along its base. In what order must this hazard be reported?

options.text: Directly to the Grand Hall in Oakhaven, followed by the local glazier and toolmaker.
To the supervising Journeyman, who escalates to the Luminary, who contacts the Master Luminary.
To the harvest crew catwalk team, who immediately notify the wagon drivers.
Directly to a Master Luminary, bypassing the Journeyman to prevent panic.

stem: How many complete harvest cycles must an Apprentice successfully finish before qualifying to sit the Shadow-Trial?

options.text: Exactly 14 cycles.
Exactly 21 cycles.
Exactly 12 cycles.
Exactly 28 cycles.

stem: What is the purpose of the sensory evaluation known as the Shadow-Trial?

options.text: To test if an Apprentice can sweep a Lunar-Net in darkness without hitting glass panels.
To determine whether an initiate can identify three stages of nectar spoilage by smell alone.
To assess how long an Apprentice can endure exposure to fifty-five Vels without fainting.
To measure an initiate's ability to count adult moths in the canopy using peripheral vision.

stem: An Apprentice compiles their technical log for promotion review. What parameters must be documented across the 50 consecutive brewing entries?

options.text: Soak time, moon-root weight, water volume, simmer temperature, humidity, resting hours, and specific gravity.
Wagon speed, flask volume, driver name, road turnpike fees, seal imprint, and delivery time.
Chamber pressure in Torr-Pascs, net sweep velocity, Candon rating, and gauntlet thickness.
Beetle trap counts, V-Scrub concentration, roof pitch angle, and timber age.

stem: Which set of equipment is issued to an Apprentice upon induction into the Keepers' Guild?

options.text: Torr-Pasc barometer, brass torque wrench, and copper kettle.
Candon-meter, Lunar-Net, and a pair of Draft-Bellows.
Vels-Thermometer, leather gauntlets, and fifty-Dram Lumium Flask.
Sponge Trough, Gravity Drip Dispenser, and unglazed ceramic jar.

stem: Beyond sweeping canopy light, why is the Lunar-Net indispensable during a disease outbreak?

options.text: Its silk mesh conducts high voltage that kills airborne bacteria around feeding troughs.
Its static-free weave allows gentle capture of infected moths without damaging brittle wings.
Its silver threads can be shredded and dissolved in boiling water to create medicinal feed.
It can be stretched across ventilation louvers to filter out Glass-Borer Beetle grubs.

stem: A Keeper prepares to calibrate an issued Candon-meter. How is the true zero point verified on the dial?

options.text: Hold the selenium plate three feet below the high apex vents during the noon sun.
Place the sensor in unfermented nectar chilled to its 12-Vel freezing point and adjust the spring screw.
Submerge the housing in boiling mountain spring water until the indicator points to forty Vels.
Expose the lens to an open tallow candle and tighten the collar nut to 14 Candons.

stem: Which collection represents the five operational areas examined during a statutory Guild Audit?

options.text: Frame integrity, ventilation mechanics, brewing sanitation, medical readiness, and ledger accuracy.
Pack wagon wheel grease, road permits, uniform stitching, apprentice ages, and candle wax purity.
Exterior garden soil, well water depth, roof snow depth, chimney soot, and window glass thickness.
Muntin resin brands, timber harvest permits, iron nail counts, copper kettle weight, and room paint.

stem: What regulatory penalties are imposed on a facility that applies unauthorized chemical tints to south-facing glass?

options.text: A fine of one hundred Drams of sugar-sap and a written warning in the Oakhaven register.
Suspension of operating charter, forfeiture of harvest, and demotion of the presiding Keeper to Apprentice.
Mandatory transfer of fifty adult moths to a neighboring facility for three breeding cycles.
A formal order requiring all Iron-Oak beams to be repainted with copper-flower extract.

stem: A Keeper inspects the brewing station twenty-four hours ahead of an audit. What sequence ensures compliance?

options.text: Paint copper kettles with V-Scrub, seal earthenware jars with pitch, and dilute all resting casks.
Desiccate moon-root over an open flame, replace wooden bungs with brass plugs, and hide older ledgers.
Inspect copper kettles for verdigris, scrub soaking jars with boiling water, check casks for mold, and zero scales.
Empty all resting vats into floor drains, polish windows with raw sap, and recalibrate Draft-Bellows.

stem: What is the exact wording of the foundational tenet of the Keeper's Code?

options.text: The light serves the house, but the Keeper serves the moth.
The swarm brings the light, but the Guild rules the mountain.
In the cold of the heights, the harvest sustains Oakhaven.
Protect the Iron-Oak frame, and the moth will yield its fire.

stem: Why does harvesting ambient light during the tenth-month Frost Moon violate Guild ethics?

options.text: The high static in cold air shatters the quartz prismatic roof panels during sweeping.
Forcing dormant insects into flight drains depleted metabolic reserves, causing mass spring mortality.
The luminescence collected during a freeze turns into toxic acidic gas inside vacuum-sealed flasks.
Dormancy causes the moths to produce a sickly green light that cannot be sold as Grade A Lumium.

stem: A Keeper in House A shuts a shared flume damper during a heat wave, forcing 55-Vel heat into House B. How does the Guild resolve this?

options.text: Permit House A to retain control if their light output exceeds that of House B by twenty percent.
Require House B to mist their canopy with cold spring water while House A finishes harvesting.
Rule House A in violation for endangering stock, mandating shared dampers remain locked at 50 percent.
Order both facilities to release their swarms into the wild Alabaster Mountains immediately.

stem: Why is it an ethical violation to over-harvest a colony during its dormant seasonal rest period?

options.text: It deprives the town of Oakhaven of its mandatory reserve tallow candles.
It infringes Section 4 by placing commercial gain above insect survival during metabolic suspension.
It ruins the silver lattice inside the Lunar-Tinted Glass along the north wall.
It speeds up fermentation in the lower Gravity Drip Dispensers before the spring thaw.

stem: What penalty is imposed on an Apprentice who allows their issued brass tools to corrode through neglect?

options.text: Immediate expulsion from the Alabaster range without appeal.
A reduction of their daily synthetic nectar ration by half for two cycles.
Immediate assignment to disciplinary physical labor in the stone foundations.
Permanent forfeiture of their right to carry a Lunar-Net during the harvest.
